sections.markdown:
## B — Audience, level and prerequisites: signal lights, arrows, intersections, right-of-way and pedestrians
Audience: first-time Arizona drivers and permit holders preparing for the written test in English, including drivers new to flashing yellow arrows and pedestrian-activated crosswalk signals.
Why it matters to a first-timer: each arrow and flashing light demands a different action at the intersection [A02], and the law says who must yield to pedestrians and when a stop is required at a crosswalk [A03].
Level: practical recall of signal meanings and yield rules; several steady, flashing and arrow indications look alike and are easy to confuse.
Prerequisites: the freeway and lane-use pages that precede this section; this section opens the roadway and vehicle knowledge chapter.

corpus_stability.reason: The Arizona Driver License Manual carries one revision line on its contents page (Revised September 2026) and points to Arizona Revised Statutes Title 28 for current law; nothing in the selected pages signals more than one rewrite per year.
